test: Device ID and serial number are read and match the label
Firmware and bootloader version, hardware and mechanical revision are what the batch plan says
limit: exact match with the release manifest

test: Supply rails on the test points
Battery protection and NTC behave as designed
Charging from USB-C: start, current, termination, charging while the device runs
All eight buttons (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, ACTION, MODE, SELECT, START) are seen one by one and none is stuck
interface_or_equipment: diagnostic firmware (button-test screen exists in the shell), actuator or manual
limit: every button seen once; no ghost presses

test: Power switch cuts the supply as designed
Volume control changes loudness smoothly over its whole travel and is quiet at the minimum
interface_or_equipment: audio capture or microphone, diagnostic tone

test: LCD shows the full 10 x 20 field and the status column with no dead pixels and the right polarity (dark on light)
limit: no dead pixel in the visible area; positive polarity

test: LCD update rate: 10, 15, 20 and 30 frames per second are shown without tearing or ghosting that makes games unplayable
White front light: off, level 1, level 2, uniformity without hot spots
Speaker plays the test tones; no buzz, no rattle
BLE: advertises, pairs, the settings and records characteristics read and write correctly
limit: all characteristics answer; unauthorised write is refused

test: USB-C data: enumeration, DFU entry and a firmware update that succeeds
limit: update succeeds and the new version is read back

test: Recovery: an interrupted update leaves a device that can still be recovered over USB-C or SWD
interface_or_equipment: USB host, SWD probe, a deliberate interruption

test: Profile storage: the two slots survive a power cut during a write; the best score is kept
limit: previous copy intact after a cut

test: Flash CRC of the installed image
The selected games start and run for a short fixed session on the real frame rate
interface_or_equipment: diagnostic firmware or an input player (recorded sessions .bkt exist for the simulator)
